periods.notes: Under the Treaty of Gandamak (26 May 1879) the emir agreed to conduct foreign relations in accordance with British 'wishes and advice'; Afghanistan kept its own ruler and internal government. Shown as a protected state under the formal-status rule. Afghanistan declared full independence in 1919, leading to the Third Anglo-Afghan War.

Colonised by British settlers in 1650. Governed with Saint Kitts and Nevis (from 1882 in the Leeward Islands federation) until it broke away in 1967; formally a separate dependent territory from 1980. A British Overseas Territory (listed in Schedule 6 of the British Nationality Act 1981); called a crown colony, then a British Dependent Territory, until 2002.

The Trucial sheikhdoms' exclusive agreements of 1892 restricted their foreign relations to Britain (after the general treaty of 1820 and the maritime truce of 1853). The former Trucial States, initially without Ras al-Khaimah, formed the United Arab Emirates in December 1971.
British-protected status dates from the treaty of 1861, under which Britain took responsibility for Bahrain's defence and foreign relations. Independent in August 1971.

Settled by the English from 1612 and a crown colony from 1684. A British Overseas Territory (listed in Schedule 6 of the British Nationality Act 1981); called a crown colony, then a British Dependent Territory, until 2002.
Protectorate proclaimed in 1885 and extended north in 1890. Ceased to be a protectorate and became independent as Botswana on 30 September 1966.

UN trusteeship agreement approved 13 December 1946. After a UN-supervised plebiscite in February 1961, the Southern Cameroons united with the former French Cameroun in October 1961. The British mandate before 1946 is not yet mapped (see DATA_ISSUES.md #19).

Ceded to Britain in 1670 and administered as a dependency of Jamaica until Jamaican independence in 1962. A British Overseas Territory (listed in Schedule 6 of the British Nationality Act 1981); called a crown colony, then a British Dependent Territory, until 2002.
Part of British-administered Cyprus under the Cyprus Convention of 1878.
Part of British Cyprus (annexed 1914) until independence on 16 August 1960. The Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus, proclaimed in 1983, is recognised only by Turkey.
Under the Cyprus Convention of 1878, Cyprus remained under Ottoman sovereignty but was administered by Britain.
Annexed by Britain in 1914, when Britain and the Ottoman Empire went to war. Independent republic from 16 August 1960, with Britain keeping sovereignty over the Akrotiri and Dhekelia bases.

Britain proclaimed a protectorate in December 1914, after declaring war on the Ottoman Empire. Before this, Egypt was under British occupation but not formally British (see DATA_ISSUES.md #1). The declaration of 28 February 1922 ended the protectorate but reserved defence, imperial communications, foreign interests and the Sudan to Britain.
Part of British-administered Cyprus (Cyprus Convention 1878; annexed 1914).

Kept under British sovereignty by the 1960 treaties that made Cyprus independent. Before 1960 part of British Cyprus. A British Overseas Territory (listed in Schedule 6 of the British Nationality Act 1981); called a crown colony, then a British Dependent Territory, until 2002.

British control re-established in early 1833, after Buenos Aires had proclaimed sovereignty in 1820; Argentina continues to claim the islands. Occupied by Argentina during the 1982 Falklands War. A British Overseas Territory (listed in Schedule 6 of the British Nationality Act 1981); called a crown colony, then a British Dependent Territory, until 2002.
United Kingdom of Great Britain and Ireland from 1 January 1801. Northern Ireland remained in the United Kingdom after 1922.
Status already in place before 1900; shown from 1900, the start of the map. Not part of the United Kingdom: a self-governing crown dependency. Occupied by Germany from July 1940 to May 1945.
Acquired by Britain as the Gold Coast colony in 1874, which later expanded. The eastern strip of present-day Ghana was part of German Togoland until it was occupied in the First World War.

British Togoland, a League of Nations mandate from 1922 and a UN trust territory from 1946, was administered with the Gold Coast; its trusteeship ended in December 1956. Independent as Ghana on 6 March 1957.

Captured by the British during the War of the Spanish Succession and formally ceded by Spain under the Treaty of Utrecht (1713). A British Overseas Territory (listed in Schedule 6 of the British Nationality Act 1981); called a crown colony, then a British Dependent Territory, until 2002.

periods.unit: Colony and Protectorate of the Gambia
periods.notes: A small coastal colony with a protectorate over the interior, established in 1894. Independent on 18 February 1965; a republic from 24 April 1970.
Not part of the United Kingdom: a self-governing crown possession. The British Parliament purchased sovereignty in 1765.

periods.unit: Chagos Archipelago; British Indian Ocean Territory from 1965
periods.notes: A dependency of the British colony of Mauritius (from 1814) until the British Indian Ocean Territory was created in 1965. Mauritius claims sovereignty; a UK–Mauritius agreement to cede sovereignty was signed in May 2025. Still listed as a British Overseas Territory in the British Nationality Act 1981 when accessed on 27 September 2026.
Part of the United Kingdom, not a colony. Its status from December 1922 (the Irish Free State) awaits a decision on how dominions are shown; see DATA_ISSUES.md.

Occupied by Britain from 1917 and then a British mandate; an Arab government under Faisal I was established under the mandate in 1921, and an Anglo-Iraqi treaty was signed on 10 October 1922. Admitted to the League of Nations as an independent state on 3 October 1932. British military occupation before the mandate is not counted as British rule (see DATA_ISSUES.md #13).

British mandate allocated at San Remo in April 1920 (civil administration from July 1920) and approved by the League of Nations in July 1922. The mandate ended with British withdrawal in May 1948, when Israel declared independence. British military occupation before the mandate is not counted as British rule (see DATA_ISSUES.md #13).
Status already in place before 1900; shown from 1900, the start of the map. Not part of the United Kingdom: a self-governing crown dependency.

Part of the British mandate for Palestine allocated at San Remo in 1920 and confirmed by the League of Nations in July 1922; ruled by Emir Abdullah from 1921. Britain recognised Transjordan's independence in 1923 while keeping control of finance, the military and foreign affairs. Independent in May 1946. British military occupation before the mandate is not counted as British rule (see DATA_ISSUES.md #13).
Status already in place before 1900; shown from 1900, the start of the map. The British East Africa Company surrendered its charter in 1895. The protectorate became a colony in 1920.
The East Africa Protectorate became a colony and was renamed Kenya in 1920. Independent on 12 December 1963.

An 1899 treaty gave Britain control of Kuwait's foreign affairs, making it a protected state under this project's formal-status rule; it became a British protectorate proper after the outbreak of the First World War. Britain recognised Kuwait's independence on 19 June 1961.

Annexed to the British Crown in 1868 and administered by the Cape Colony until 1884, when it came under direct British rule as one of three High Commission Territories. The Lesotho Independence Act 1966 calls it the Colony of Basutoland. Independent as Lesotho on 4 October 1966.
A British protectorate, formalised in 1887. Independent in July 1965; the last British troops left on 29 March 1976.
Captured from France in 1800 and kept by Britain under the 1814 Treaty of Paris. Independent in September 1964; a republic from 13 December 1974.

English colony from 1632, returned to Britain by the Treaty of Paris (1783) after the last French capture. Part of the Leeward Islands federal colony 1871–1956 and the West Indies Federation 1958–62. A British Overseas Territory (listed in Schedule 6 of the British Nationality Act 1981); called a crown colony, then a British Dependent Territory, until 2002.
Proclaimed a British colony in 1814 under the Treaty of Paris. Independent in March 1968.

periods.unit: British Central Africa Protectorate; Nyasaland from 1907
periods.notes: Protectorate established in 1891; called the British Central Africa Protectorate from 1893 and Nyasaland from 1907. Part of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, 1953–1963. Independent on 6 July 1964.

Captured from Germany by South African troops in 1914–15 and mandated to South Africa in 1920. Shown as British only while South Africa itself counts as British (to the Statute of Westminster, 1931). South Africa kept control until Namibian independence on 21 March 1990.

periods.unit: Protectorates of Northern and Southern Nigeria; Lagos Colony
periods.notes: The Royal Niger Company's charter was abrogated on 1 January 1900, leaving British protectorates in the north and south alongside the colony of Lagos (a separate colony since 1886). The northern Cameroons, now part of Nigeria, was German until the First World War.
The two protectorates were amalgamated on 1 January 1914 as the Colony and Protectorate of Nigeria; the colony was Lagos, the rest a protectorate. Independent on 1 October 1960.
The northern part of the British Cameroons trust territory remained British after Nigerian independence and joined Nigeria's Northern region in June 1961, after a UN-supervised plebiscite.

Settled by the Bounty mutineers in 1790 and placed under the British high commissioner for the Western Pacific in 1898; administered from Fiji from 1952, and by the high commissioner in New Zealand from 1970. A British Overseas Territory (listed in Schedule 6 of the British Nationality Act 1981); called a crown colony, then a British Dependent Territory, until 2002.

Part of Mandatory Palestine: allocated to Britain at San Remo in April 1920 and approved by the League of Nations in July 1922, until British withdrawal in May 1948. British military occupation before the mandate is not counted as British rule (see DATA_ISSUES.md #13).
A 1916 treaty gave Britain control of Qatar's foreign policy in return for British protection. Independent on 3 September 1971.
Anglo-Egyptian Condominium declared in 1899: sovereignty shared by the khedive of Egypt and the British Crown. Self-government agreed in 1953; independent in January 1956.
Part of the Anglo-Egyptian Sudan (condominium declared in 1899). South Sudan became independent from Sudan in 2011.

territories.name: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands

periods.unit: South Georgia and the South Sandwich Islands
periods.notes: Formally annexed by Britain in 1908. Briefly occupied by Argentina in 1982. A British Overseas Territory (listed in Schedule 6 of the British Nationality Act 1981); called a crown colony, then a British Dependent Territory, until 2002.

territories.name: Saint Helena, Ascension and Tristan da Cunha

periods.unit: Saint Helena, with Ascension and Tristan da Cunha
periods.notes: Status already in place before 1900; shown from 1900, the start of the map. Saint Helena has been British since the English East India Company took possession in 1659. Ascension became its dependency in 1922. A British Overseas Territory (listed in Schedule 6 of the British Nationality Act 1981); called a crown colony, then a British Dependent Territory, until 2002.
Status already in place before 1900; shown from 1900, the start of the map. A coastal colony (Freetown) with a much larger protectorate inland. Independent on 27 April 1961.

Status already in place before 1900; shown from 1900, the start of the map. Evacuated in 1940 during the Second World War and recaptured in 1941. Independent on 26 June 1960, then united with the former Italian Somaliland to form Somalia.
British colonial administration from 1906 as a High Commission Territory; formally a protected state from 1967. Ceased to be a protected state on 6 September 1968.
Ceded to Britain by the Treaty of Paris (1814) and administered as a dependency of Mauritius until it became a separate crown colony in 1903. Self-government in 1975; independent in June 1976.

Annexed by the Bahamas government in 1799. Under the governor of Jamaica 1874–1959 and a separate crown colony from 1962; for a time in the 1960s and 70s under the Bahamas. A British Overseas Territory (listed in Schedule 6 of the British Nationality Act 1981); called a crown colony, then a British Dependent Territory, until 2002.
Zanzibar was proclaimed a British protectorate in 1890. The mainland was German East Africa until the First World War.
League of Nations mandate under the Treaty of Versailles (in force January 1920); placed under UN trusteeship in 1947. Zanzibar remained a separate British protectorate throughout.
Tanganyika became independent in December 1961. Zanzibar became independent on 10 December 1963 and merged with Tanganyika on 26 April 1964.

Status already in place before 1900; shown from 1900, the start of the map. A protectorate was declared over Buganda in 1894 and extended to the rest of present-day Uganda. Independent in October 1962.

Annexed to the British-administered Leeward Islands in 1672; a crown colony after the Leeward Islands federation was dissolved (1956) and its governorship abolished (1960). Became an overseas territory under the British Overseas Territories Act 2002.
Part of British-administered Cyprus (Cyprus Convention 1878; annexed 1914).

Kept under British sovereignty by the 1960 treaties that made Cyprus independent. Before 1960 part of British Cyprus. A British Overseas Territory (listed in Schedule 6 of the British Nationality Act 1981); called a crown colony, then a British Dependent Territory, until 2002.

periods.unit: Aden, with the Aden Protectorate states
periods.notes: Status already in place before 1900; shown from 1900, the start of the map. Aden was taken by Britain in 1839, governed from British India until 1937 and then a crown colony. It was surrounded by 21 British protectorate states, all but four of which had joined the Federation of South Arabia by 1965; Aden joined in 1963. Sovereignty was transferred to the National Liberation Front on 30 November 1967, creating South Yemen.

The British colonies of the Cape and Natal (Natal self-governing from 1893). The Transvaal and Orange Free State were Boer republics at war with Britain; Britain proclaimed the annexation of the Transvaal in 1900, but the war ended only with the Treaty of Vereeniging on 31 May 1902.

periods.unit: Cape Colony, Natal, Transvaal and Orange River Colony
periods.notes: Four British colonies after the Treaty of Vereeniging. Natal was self-governing from 1893; the former republics received responsible government in 1906–07.

The Union of South Africa, a British dominion created by the South Africa Act 1909, was formed on 31 May 1910. British status ends with the Statute of Westminster (11 December 1931) under this project's rule. South Africa became a republic and left the Commonwealth on 31 May 1961.

periods.unit: North-Eastern and North-Western Rhodesia; Northern Rhodesia from 1911
periods.notes: Status already in place before 1900; shown from 1900, the start of the map. Administered by the British South Africa Company (chartered 1889), at first in two parts, united as Northern Rhodesia in 1911.

The company handed administration to the Colonial Office in 1924. Part of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, 1953–1963. Ceased to be a protectorate and became independent as Zambia on 24 October 1964.
Status already in place before 1900; shown from 1900, the start of the map. The British South Africa Company received its royal charter in October 1889.
Annexed to the Crown as a self-governing colony on 12 September 1923. Part of the Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland, 1953–1963.

The white minority government's Unilateral Declaration of Independence (11 November 1965) was not recognised; the Southern Rhodesia Act 1965 declared the territory still part of Her Majesty's dominions. In practice ruled by the Rhodesian government until Britain resumed control in 1979. Independent as Zimbabwe on 18 April 1980.
